summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Mucous glands secrete mucin to keep skin moist for cutaneous gas exchange. Poison glands secrete defensive toxins. Skin is shed periodically during Moulting.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SKIN HISTOLOGY OF FROG
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
EPIDERMIS (Outer Layer)                                     DERMIS (Inner Layer)
├── Stratum Corneum (Keratinized, cast off during moulting)  ├── Stratum Spongiosum (Vascularized)
└── Stratum Germinativum (Mitotic basal Malpighian layer)    │   ├── Mucous Glands (Moisture)
                                                             │   └── Poison Glands (Defense)
                                                             └── Stratum Compactum (Connective)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The integument (skin) of *Rana tigrina* is thin, moist, smooth, slippery, and loosely attached to the underlying musculature by subcutaneous lymphatic spaces (**Lymph Sacs**).

### 1. Epidermis (Ectodermal Origin)
• **Stratum Corneum**: Outermost, thin, dead, cornified layer composed of flattened keratinized cells. Periodically shed in fragments along with skin cast off (**Moulting**).
• **Stratum Germinativum (Malpighian Layer)**: Innermost living layer of columnar cells undergoing continuous mitotic division to replenish the stratum corneum.

### 2. Dermis (Mesodermal Origin)
• **Stratum Spongiosum**: Upper loose connective tissue layer containing dense blood capillary networks, chromatophores, and cutaneous glands.
• **Stratum Compactum**: Lower dense layer of collagen and elastic fibers running parallel to the body surface.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 2.1 Cutaneous Glands & Chromatophore Dynamics
conceptBreakdown.title: 2.1 Cutaneous Glands & Chromatophore Dynamics
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Mucous Glands**: Simple saccular multicellular exocrine glands opening onto the epidermal surface. Secrete a watery, slippery mucin that keeps the skin permanently moist—a non-negotiable prerequisite for cutaneous gas exchange.
• **Poison Glands**: Larger, less abundant saccular glands producing a white, milky, bitter acrid fluid providing defense against predators.
• **Chromatophores** (Pigment Cells):
  - **Melanophores**: Contain dark brown/black melanin granules.
  - **Xanthophores / Erythrophores**: Contain yellow/red carotenoid pigments.
  - **Iridophores**: Contain reflective guanine crystals producing iridescence.
